body:
# Purpose / Goal

`XMLValidator.validate` reports "XML declaration allowed only at the start of the document." for a declaration before the root, but accepts one inside an element:

Input:
```js
XMLValidator.validate('<foo><?xml version="1.0"?></foo>')
XMLValidator.validate('<foo>bar<?xml?></foo>')
```
Expected: `InvalidXml` error, "XML declaration allowed only at the start of the document."
Actual: `true` for both. libxml2 rejects both documents.

Cause: inside tag content the validator calls `readPI(xmlData, ++i)`, which passes the index of the `?` instead of the index after `<?`. `readPI` then reads the target as `?xml`, so the `tagname === 'xml'` check never matches. The top-level call already passes the position after `<?`; this change does the same in tag content.

# Type
* [x] Bug Fix
* [ ] Refactoring / Technology upgrade
* [ ] New Feature

Testing:
- The new spec in `spec/validator_spec.js` fails before the change and passes after.
- `npx jasmine "spec/*spec.js"`: 333 specs, 0 failures, 2 pending.
- The benchmarks in `benchmark/` exercise the parser and builder, not the validator, so I did not include perf numbers. The change only alters an index argument.
- `lib/` and the changelog are left for the maintainers, per CONTRIBUTING.
title: fix: validator; reject an XML declaration inside an element

body: # Purpose / Goal `XMLValidator.validate()` rejects well-formed documents that contain an entity reference whose name has `-` or `.` in it, so `parser.parse(xml, true)` (validate, then parse) throws on input the parser itself handles fine. **Input** ```js const xml = ']>&foo-bar;'; ``` **Expected output** ```js XMLValidator.validate(xml); // true new XMLParser().parse(xml, true); // { a: "hello" } ``` **Actual output (before this change)** ```js XMLValidator.validate(xml); // { err: { code: "InvalidChar", msg: "char '&' is not expected.", line: 1, col: 46 } } new XMLParser().parse(xml); // { a: "hello" } (without validation) new XMLParser().parse(xml, true); // throws ``` **Cause**: `validateAmpersand` in `src/validator.js` only accepted `\w` characters in an entity name. Per the XML spec an entity name is a `Name`, which allows `-`, `.`, `:` and non-ASCII letters after the first character, and `DocTypeReader` already accepts such names. **Change**: `validateAmpersand` now accepts any XML `NameChar` (new `isNameChar` helper in `src/util.js`, built from the same `nameChar` set that `isName` already uses). The existing 20 character limit and the first-character leniency are unchanged, so every input accepted before is still accepted. **Tests**: added a spec to `spec/validator_spec.js` (names with `-`, `.`, `:`, a non-ASCII letter, the DOCTYPE example above, and negative cases for a space, `+`, and a missing `;`). It fails before the change; `npm test` (333 specs, 0 failures) and `npm run test-types` pass. **Perf** (`XMLValidator.validate` on a ~270 KB document with many `&`/`<`/`{` references, median of 5 runs of 50): 2.42 ms before, 2.10 ms after. I did not run `benchmark/XmlParser.mjs`, which needs its own dependency install. Notes: changelog, version and bundles are left to maintainers per the contributing guide. `npm run lint` already reports errors on master (and its `benchmark/**/*.js` glob matches no files); the one new report from this change is the same `no-misleading-character-class` that `src/util.js` already triggers for `nameStartChar`. # Type * [x] Bug Fix * [ ] Refactoring / Technology upgrade * [ ] New Feature
title: fix: validator; accept XML name characters in entity references

body:
# Purpose / Goal

Keep the current stop node in the path matcher until `updateTag` has run. It is currently popped first, so the callback receives the parent's path. With `jPath: false`, matcher predicates also inspect the parent instead of the stop node. Path-based skipping and renaming therefore fail when combined with `stopNodes`.

No existing issue describes this exact case, so here is a reproduction as requested by the PR template:

```js
const parser = new XMLParser({
  stopNodes: ['root.skip'],
  updateTag: (tagName, jPath) => jPath === 'root.skip' ? false : tagName
});
parser.parse('<root><skip><nested/></skip><keep>ok</keep></root>');
```

Actual: `{ root: { skip: '<nested/>', keep: 'ok' } }`

Expected: `{ root: { keep: 'ok' } }`

The fix moves `addChild`, which invokes `updateTag`, before the matcher pop. It leaves the raw stop-node content and subsequent sibling paths unchanged.

# Tests

- Four new regression cases fail on the unchanged source and pass with this fix.
- Coverage includes path-based skipping/renaming in both output modes, self-closing and unpaired stop nodes, matcher attribute predicates with `jPath: false`, and following siblings.
- `npm test`: 336 specs, 0 failures, 2 existing pending specs on Node 24.19.0.
- Full Jasmine suite also passes on Node 14 and Node 22: 336 specs, 0 failures, 2 existing pending specs.
- `npm run test-types`: passes.
- `git diff --check`: passes.
- `npm run lint` is blocked on both baseline and final source because `benchmark/**/*.js` matches no files. Focused ESLint with ECMAScript 2022 reports only the same existing unused variables in the two files.

# Performance

Ran the documented `node benchmark/XmlParser.mjs` before and after on the same shared VM. Requests/second in the consecutive comparison:

| Parser | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| fxp | 33,757 | 34,356 |
| fxp, preserve order | 40,447 | 41,447 |

These are noisy single-run observations, not a performance claim. The default benchmark does not use stop nodes; this change only reorders the existing callback and matcher pop in the stop-node branch.

# Type

* [x] Bug Fix
* [ ] Refactoring / Technology upgrade
* [ ] New Feature
title: fix: preserve stop-node paths in updateTag callbacks

body: # Purpose / Goal Self-closing tags go through `transformTagName` twice: once before the trailing `/` is stripped, so the callback receives e.g. `a/`, and again in the self-closing branch. Lowercase or map transforms hide it. With a non-idempotent one they don't: ```js new XMLParser({ transformTagName: n => 'ns_' + n }).parse('') // actual: {"ns_root":{"ns_a":"","ns_ns_a":""}} // expected: {"ns_root":{"ns_a":["",""]}} ``` This strips the `/` before the single transform call and removes the second call, so each tag is transformed once with its real name. Two side effects of the move: - `strictReservedNames` now also rejects `<#text/>`. Before, it produced `{"r":[]}`, while `<#text>` and `<#text a="1"/>` already threw. - With a non-idempotent transform and `allowBooleanAttributes`, `` no longer keeps `@_a`. It only had it because the doubled name made `tagName !== tagExp`; without a transform it is already dropped. That is a separate bug in the attribute check, not touched here. Added a spec covering paired, empty and attributed self-closing tags. `npm test` passes (333 specs) on Node 22 and 14. # Type * [x] Bug Fix * [ ] Refactoring / Technology upgrade * [ ] New Feature Written with AI assistance (Claude); I have reviewed the change.
title: fix: apply transformTagName once to self-closing tags

body:
### Description

`XMLValidator` already rejects documents with more than one root node, but the check is skipped whenever one of the roots is self closing:

```js
const { XMLValidator } = require('fast-xml-parser');

XMLValidator.validate('<xml></xml><xml2></xml2>'); // error: Multiple possible root nodes found.  ✅
XMLValidator.validate('<xml/><xml2/>');            // true  ❌
XMLValidator.validate('<xml></xml><xml2/>');       // true  ❌
XMLValidator.validate('<test><nested/></test><xml2/>'); // true  ❌
XMLValidator.validate('<xml/>extra');              // true  ❌  ('<xml></xml>extra' is rejected)
```

All of these are not well-formed XML — a document has exactly one root element — and the validator's own error messages (`Multiple possible root nodes found.`, `Extra text at the end`) exist for precisely these cases.

### Root cause

In `src/validator.js`:

* `reachedRoot = true` is only assigned in the closing-tag branch, when popping a tag empties the stack. A self closing tag never reaches that branch, so it never ends the root level — hence `'<xml/>extra'` and `'<xml/><xml2/>'` pass.
* The `Multiple possible root nodes found.` check lives only in the branch for a paired opening tag, so a self closing tag after a completed root is never checked — hence `'<xml></xml><xml2/>'` passes.

### Fix

In the self closing branch, once the attributes validate, treat a tag with an empty stack as a root node: report the multiple-root error if a root was already seen, otherwise mark the root level as reached. Nested self closing tags (`<test><nested/></test>`) are unaffected because the stack is not empty there.

### Tests

Added to `spec/validator_spec.js`:

* multiple roots with the first root self closing, the second root self closing, and a self closing root after a root with nested tags
* a single self closing root (with and without attributes) and nested self closing tags stay valid
* text after a self closing root is rejected, trailing whitespace is still allowed

4 of the new specs fail without the source change. The full suite passes with it (`npx jasmine spec/*spec.js` → 338 specs, 0 failures, 2 pending).
title: fix: validator accepts multiple root nodes when a root is self closing

Introduce new option `initialIndentationLevel` and initialize `builder` with it instead of the literal value `0`.
